WORKLOG / DOSSIER - task 0 (home_loan_servicing), frozen 2026-10-08 10:20:00 EDT. Rework round 2 after the policy-task audit (audits/policy_task/home_loan_servicing/0.md, _difficulty.md).

[Step 0 - draw] draw_counts.py --task 0 -> {"prerequisite_problems": 3, "problems": 4, "factor_counts": [4, 5, 4, 6]}. Assignment: deferment fee 6, good-faith payment 5, escrow analysis 4, returned-payment fee 4.

[Scope snapshot] First task. Claimed: loan_ext_escrow_analysis, loan_ext_returned_payment_fee, loan_ext_good_faith_payment, loan_ext_deferment_fee with tools issue_escrow_analysis_2b6c143e, assess_returned_payment_fee_86f751f1, make_good_faith_payment_f58b4303, sign_deferment_agreement_a442f6a7. Task 1 keeps the late charge, payoff statement and sale paydown tree; the two scopes are disjoint and together cover the seven policies.

[Why a good test] A borrower in hardship asks only to move September and October to the end of the loan. The deferment fee waits on an escrow analysis dated within twelve months (last 2025-09-30), a returned-payment fee on every fee-bearing return (the 2026-10-06 account_closed return has none) and a good-faith partial payment received on the signing date (suspense 0.00). The agent reads the three prerequisite sentences, finds each unmet in the records, works out which write brings each state about, and then computes the fee, whose scheduled installment and risk add-on move with two of those writes.

[Problem-tree card] root loan_ext_deferment_fee (owner user).
 edge 1 -> loan_ext_escrow_analysis: value_input, gate installment, state form, "The deferment fee is fixed only after the loan carries an escrow analysis dated within the twelve months before the signing date."; false at opening: initial_state.loan_notices.966adea6-072b-45f1-a928-acf11897344f.notice_date = 2025-09-30; only the escrow-analysis tool records analyses.
 edge 2 -> loan_ext_returned_payment_fee: value_input, gate returned_fees_12m, state form, "Before the deferment fee is fixed, the fees owed on the loan must carry a returned-payment fee for every payment returned for a fee-bearing reason."; false: return e9d7d23b-564a-4bdd-8418-f58566d4ef1e (account_closed, source fcea0644-fe6f-4ae4-90b0-f75731273def) has no fee; only the returned-payment-fee tool books such fees.
 edge 3 -> loan_ext_good_faith_payment: state_gate, gate loan_holdings.suspense_balance, state form, "The deferment agreement is not signed until a good-faith partial payment received on the signing date stands in suspense."; false: suspense 0.00, no partial payment today; only the good-faith tool books partial payments. The good-faith rule no longer restates the order (audit O-1): it defines the payment as "a one-time partial payment the borrower authorizes on their own loan toward a hardship deferment".
 Four-point test: connectives "only after" / "Before ... must" / "not ... until"; record-visible states; no tool/id/code token; hard requirement. Directions mixed.
 Order: the three prerequisites in any order (6 orders run: identical arguments, one terminal hash), then the deferment. Deletion runs: skip analysis -> 62.09; skip returned-payment fee -> 57.59; skip good-faith -> 62.61 with the partial-payment row missing (state gate).

[Base-invariant card] loan_deferment_terms: program_offers_deferment (20-Year: true), deferment_loan_open (delinquent allowed); 55 installments paid >= 12; 37 days past due <= 59; no agreement in the trailing 12 months; 2 <= 2 per request; lifetime room 6 - 1 = 5 (now inside installments_deferred, audit O-12). loan_evt_payment_application: loan_open_for_payments; 240.68 stays below one installment so it is held in suspense. loan_escrow_terms: no structured gate. loan_evt_returned_payment: the once-only gate concerns the return, recorded once. No time gate (temporal_feasibility []).

[Business-object card] Loan 4e182d5a-bb47-4053-8e83-086a24867d20. Fee object: return e9d7d23b-564a-4bdd-8418-f58566d4ef1e -> payment fcea0644-fe6f-4ae4-90b0-f75731273def; excluded: the 2026-09-03 and 2025-10-03 returns already carry fees. Deferred objects: installments 2026-09-01 and 2026-10-01. Late charge 43.30 on 2026-09-01 was assessed 2026-09-17; 2026-10-01 is still in grace.

[Factor card] (tier; evidence; single-factor baseline from the sensitivity run)
 escrow analysis = 92.73 (all-baseline 80.97): projection source (method: offer 1059 vs policy premium vs ledger) -> 71.83; cushion 1 month (parameter) -> 96.41; deposit window (method: from the oldest unpaid due date) -> 98.72; shortage spread 24 (parameter; audit CG-1 fixed: tiers now split on a shortage of at least one month's projection, so the 12-month fall-through is what a small shortage gets) -> 97.22.
 returned-payment fee = 35.0 (all-baseline 30.0): channel 20.00 -> 50.0; window 24 months (method) -> 30.0; repeat 1.5 -> 25.0; reason 5.00 -> 30.0.
 good-faith payment = 240.68 (all-baseline 455.84): percentage 40 -> 150.43; installment window (method; audit CG-4/T0-2 fixed: a counting convention by loan seasoning replaces the multiplier-labelled factor) -> 481.36; repeat 1.2 -> 200.57; payment history 1.1 -> 218.8; standing fraction 0.5 (now labelled parameter) -> 481.36.
 deferment fee = 62.61 (all-baseline 70.09): agreement 30.00 -> 87.61; repeat 1.25 (agreement within 36 months AND deferred months, audit O-10) -> 55.11; rate 0.75 -> 67.63; add-on 0.50 -> 52.57; periods 4 (method) -> 50.06; relationship fraction 0.5 (now parameter) -> 87.72.
 Counts: escrow 2 parameter / 2 method; returned fee 3/1; good-faith 4/1; deferment 5/1. Multi-source: cushion, count window, payment history, standing, repeat factor. Cross-difficulty: insurance (projection, cushion, relationship), lease (agreement charge, standing), utility (standing). Near-misses: older renewal offers; the 2022-11-12 premium (46 months); the 2025-10-03 return and fee (12 months 5 days).

[Revision R3 - audit round 2]
 CG-5 / T0-4: the good-faith installment window's tiers were re-cut on loan seasoning so all three are reachable by a borrower who can take a hardship deferment (12 or more installments paid means 12 or more months since the first installment): 48 or more months -> only installments a whole month or more past due; fewer than 24 months -> also the next installment; 24-47 months -> every unpaid installment due by the payment date (the standard, also the baseline). A deferment-eligible loan 13-23 months old reaches the 'fewer than 24' tier, one 24-47 months old the fall-through. This world (57 months) takes the 48+ tier; every figure is unchanged (240.68; window baseline 481.36), and the 2024-02-20 historical payment (25 months) stays on the fall-through.
[Rounding] Every amount is now rounded half up in compute (int(RND(x * 100, 6) + 0.5) / 100), matching the rule text (audit O-6/T0-3); the three disputed proof figures are recomputed under it.

[Overrides] escrow analysis: two loan_escrow_terms clauses; returned-payment fee: the nsf_fee sentence; deferment fee: the deferment_fee sentence; good-faith payment: none. Escrow-analysis wording of the deposit window now states the whole-months convention the compute uses (audit O-2).

[Seed design] Full loan history since funding (142 transactions, 5 notices); historical rows recomputed under the revised charter (2023-09-30 analysis now spreads its small shortage over 12; 2024 good-faith 136.75 and deferment fee 36.24 with half-up rounding). The 2026 renewal offer is 1059 (dwelling raised to 117,500 at renewal with the age band 6-10 and no claims-free discount after the 2026 claim: 117.5 x 9.80 x 0.92 = 1059). Opening obligations carried here: the overdue analysis and the 2026-10-06 return's fee. Not owed: late charge on 2026-10-01 (in grace), right-to-cure (37 < 45), suspense application.

[Persona] unchanged from round 1 (goal, bounced draft and closed-account mix-up as opening facts; passive reactions; payment and signature only on hand-over; closes after the deferment).

[Standard solution] locate by phone -> verify (phone + DOB) -> read loan, transactions, notices, lease, utility, insurance policy and notices -> escrow analysis 92.73 / shortage 107.58 / surplus 0.00 -> returned-payment fee 35.00 on fcea0644-fe6f-4ae4-90b0-f75731273def -> good-faith payment 240.68 (borrower) -> deferment 2 installments, fee 62.61 (borrower).

[Draft recomputation from visible context] Each rule's prose with the listed rows gives the same objects, order and values.

[Gate results - final run, repository root, no --task]
 check_extended: EXTENDED OK; check_task_tools: TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK; replay_tasks: REPLAY OK (0.json deterministic, non-vacuous, closure = initial); check_solvability: SOLVABILITY OK; check_compute: COMPUTE OK; check_grounding: GROUNDING OK; check_cross_fire: SCOPE OK; check_cache_diff: info only. check_traceability deferred to render.
user_scenario:
You are Rosalind M. Nakamura, 69, a retired school-cafeteria manager who owns her manufactured home on site C-327 at Palmetto Shores, the Hearthstone community in Fort Myers, Florida; you bought the home new in 2021 with a loan from Hearthstone Home Finance. This summer your husband Glenn had heart surgery, you have been driving him to rehab and covering co-pays, and money has been tight. The automatic draft for your September loan payment bounced, and when you tried to catch up by phone on October 2nd you read out the number of the old checking account you had already closed, so that payment came back too; October's payment hasn't been made either. You are calling the resident desk to ask whether your September and October loan payments can be moved to the end of the loan, the way you understand a hardship deferment works, and you would like it done today if you qualify. You speak warmly but a little anxiously and apologize for the mix-up with the old account.
When the representative asks who you are, you give your phone number, 239-555-0146. If they need more to confirm your identity you give your date of birth, June 14, 1957 (1957-06-14); if they still need another detail, the last four of your Social Security number, 3342. You give your email, rosalind.nakamura@gmail.com, only if they ask for it. You don't remember your loan number and say they should be able to find it under your name or phone number. If asked why you need the deferment, you explain Glenn's surgery and that his disability checks should start in November, so you expect to be back on track then.
You don't know how the loan's figures are worked out and you don't guess at them. If the representative explains that something has to be taken care of on the account first, you tell them that's fine and to go ahead. If they tell you a payment has to be made today before the deferment can be signed, you say you can pay it from your new checking account at Suncoast; when they hand that payment over for you to make yourself, you make it for exactly the amount and loan number they give you and read back the confirmation number you get. When they hand you the deferment agreement to sign yourself, you sign it for exactly the number of payments and the fee they tell you. Once they tell you the deferment is signed and when your next payment is due, you thank them and say goodbye; you have nothing else to ask.
